text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- The contract for Die Erste savings bank's takeover of Bank Austria's stake in GiroCredit is ready to be signed, Bank Austria's chief Gerhard Randa says.

- Interior Minister Karl Schloegl says he plans to work together with the EU Commission and aid organisations on helping at least half the Bosnian refugees return to their home country or become integrated in Austria by the summer.
- Vienna's Philharmonic Orchestra has allowed the first female musician to join the former male bastion. Anna Lelkes, a harpist, has now officially become the orchestra's first female member.
- Steelmaker VA Stahl's chief executive Franz Strutzl expects the company's workforce to fall 20 percent in the longer term.
- Siemens Austria plans to cut 300 jobs at its cable production due to lower sales. The dividend remains unchanged at 26 schillings.
- Insurer Anker-Versicherung's pre-tax premium earnings jumped 22.9 percent to 2.798 billion schillings in 1996.
- Austria's industry sees itself incapable of creating more jobs.
- Austria's tourism industry reports stagnating sales this winter. Turnover was up a nominal 1.3 percent.
- Chancellor Viktor Klima will announce new plans for apprentices at the weekend as industry complains about the deteriorating education and the number of open apprentice jobs does not meet demand.
- Transport Minister Caspar Einem will have to work on the new telecommunications law as criticism on the draft law is growing.
- Some employees at postal savings bank PSK prefer Bawag to become the new minority shareholder, while others favour Die Erste and GiroCredit.
